reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general fusion material challenges and simulation methods but provides no specific data on carbide formation in WTaCrV alloys, the role of TaC as defect sinks, or the link between precipitation and hardening in this system. premises: Trace carbon addition (~0.3 at%) during consolidation forms finely dispersed TaC carbides in W38Ta36Cr15V11.
TaC carbides act as stable defect sinks and grain boundary pinning points.
Defect sinks and grain boundary pinning suppress radiation-induced Cr/V precipitation.
Suppressing precipitation maintains negligible irradiation hardening.
